issues: Post-prandial afternoon hyperglycemia peaks reaching up to 290 mg/dL driven by unannounced meals and closed-loop UAM response.
Moderate nocturnal time below range (up to 18.5% between 00:00 and 02:00 local time) and overall hypoglycemia frequency of 5.1% <70 mg/dL.
Complete absence of logged carbohydrate entries in treatment data, forcing closed-loop automation to rely entirely on reactive UAM microbolusing.
summary: The 14-day analysis demonstrates strong overall glycemic control with an 86.0% Time in Range, supported by robust OpenAPS closed-loop automation (SMB and UAM enabled). However, the complete lack of logged carbohydrate entries forces the algorithm to reactively manage unannounced meals, leading to afternoon hyperglycemia peaks and subsequent late hypoglycemia risk (5.1% <70 mg/dL). Baseline profile settings are generally effective, but safety and meal strategy adjustments are needed before modifying core profile parameters.
education: Unannounced meal (UAM) handling allows closed-loop systems to respond to unexpected rises, but prebolusing or logging carbohydrates significantly reduces post-prandial peaks and late insulin stacking.
Maintaining a wide maximum IOB limit relative to total daily dose increases the risk of aggressive stacking when unannounced rises coincide with dynamic sensitivity adjustments.
strengths: High CGM data coverage (98.7%) with stable telemetry and consistent closed-loop operation.
Effective overnight fasting stability across early morning hours.
Well-configured Oref1 automation features including active dynamic ISF and microbolusing.
safety_notes: TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice.
This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of explicit carb entries restricts exact post-prandial evaluation.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal and targets maintain stable fasting glucose, while afternoon highs are driven by unannounced meals.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly glucose local data shows stable overnight averages (90–106 mg/dL) and afternoon peaks up to 162.8 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of recorded carb entries prevents direct isolation of post-prandial insulin requirements.

analysis_steps.evidence: ISF segment 56 mg/dL/U, dynamic ISF factor 70%, 10-hour DIA.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of carb entries blocks validation of carb ratios.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: No declared meal entries to contrast announced versus unannounced delivery.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: No extended carb entries or structured meal absorption overrides.

analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesis of data quality, safety, basal stability, and automation settings.

recommendations.title: Review Max IOB Safety Limit
recommendations.description: The current max IOB limit of 25 U is wide relative to total daily dose (~20 U/day), representing a potential stacking risk during unannounced excursions.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight and fasting basal segments maintain stable glucose control, and existing variations are adequately managed by closed-loop automation.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe glucose behavior for 5-7 days after introducing consistent manual meal carb logging before evaluating profile changes.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Introduce consistent manual carbohydrate entry and modest prebolusing for meals to give the closed-loop algorithm advance notice, reducing reliance on reactive UAM microboluses and smoothing out post-prandial spikes.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Without declared carbohydrates, the closed-loop system relies entirely on UAM and SMB to catch rises post-facto, causing initial hyperglycemia followed by late insulin over-delivery and hypoglycemia risk.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record explicit carbohydrate entries and meal times for a 3-to-5-day observation window to evaluate closed-loop performance under announced conditions.

exceptions.suggestion: Keep current overnight closed-loop settings without intervention.
exceptions.rationale: Fasting stability is strong during nocturnal hours.

exceptions.suggestion: Apply a short prebolus or manual announcement before afternoon meals.
exceptions.rationale: Afternoon windows show the highest glucose peaks and variability.

implementation_steps: 1. Review current max IOB settings against total daily insulin requirements with the care team.
2. Begin logging meal carbohydrate entries consistently for 3 to 5 days without altering basal or ISF parameters.
3. Evaluate post-prandial glycemic response and review time in range and time below range before considering profile adjustments.
